subject: scorpion
pitch: A desert scorpion in a threatening pose, tail arched high over its back. Glossy amber armour with darker bands at every joint, big crab-like pincers held forward, eight thin legs, a segmented tail ending in a bulbous dark stinger, and a cluster of tiny black eyes on the head shield.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module using the SDK to model a scorpion, thinking through realistic proportions—roughly a 10-12 cm body with a tail—while keeping the implementation moderate in scope and relying on APIs I'm confident are correct.

I'm working out the scorpion's orientation and tail pose, deciding it faces +Z with the tail arching up from the rear and curling forward over the body toward a stinger point, giving it a threatening posture.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton structure, starting with a root pelvis joint and building a spine chain outward from there.

Still writing joint hierarchy...

I'll place the sphere bulb at the tail's endpoint frame for the stinger tip, then add a sharper small cone near the end to suggest a pointed stinger shape.

For the banding along the tail, I'm considering a color function or banded segments to alternate amber and dark stripes at the joints, giving it a segmented insect-like look.

For legs, I'm thinking of eight thin limbs built from body side points to foot targets on the ground plane, spread four per side, using a limb or chain helper with bends to get a natural stance.

The hint vector just needs to be normalized for direction. Each limb call returns a three-point path (root, knee, foot), so I need to pass three names to the chain builder to get hip, knee, and tip joints properly labeled.

Settling on prefixed names like legL1hip, legL1knee, legL1foot to keep them unique across limbs, parented to the core joint, then sweeping the chain with a tapered radius for a dark-colored leg. For the pincers, I'm sketching a curved arm path from shoulder to wrist using a few control points, planning to build it as its own named chain for the claw mechanism.

Defining finger paths...

Adding a dark tip sphere for the claw, then shaping the palm with a box geometry attached to the hand bone, positioning it relative to the hand's coordinate frame.

I'll give the head shield a non-uniform scale to flatten it into a dome shape, then add the eyes as a tiny cluster of black spheres positioned on the front-top of the head using local directional offsets like left, up, and forward.

Now I'm planning the body: a spherical prosoma, then a segmented abdomen made of scaled ellipsoid spheres arranged along the z-axis with slight offsets between each segment to suggest joints.

For the joint bands between segments, I'm adding thin dark torus rings whose natural orientation (lying flat with axis along Z) already wraps correctly around the body's long axis, so no extra rotation is needed—just sizing the radius and tube thickness to approximate each segment's width.

For materials, I'm sticking with the fixed roughness and using the amber, dark, and black palette already chosen, and I'm deciding ground scenery isn't necessary. I'm checking that the lowest contact points—feet, pincers, tail stinger—all sit near y=0 for a stable stance, with overall height around 0.3m, then working out how to call the leg-building helper, figuring out the right way to pass bend directions for the knee joint.

Now I'm working through the naming scheme for leg joints and chains, using L/R side labels and index numbers to keep hip, knee, and foot names consistent, and setting up the mirrored side using a sign value to pick left versus right. I'm sketching the pincer arm path as a curved set of points.

Defining more joints and chain names...

Adding a dark sphere at the finger tip for contrast, then working on the tail: I'm tracing a curved path from the abdomen's rear that arches up and forward, placing the stinger tip above and ahead of the body near the head, and building that as a chained segment structure for the tail bones.

For the tail's taper, I'm shrinking the radius from base to tip, then adding a bulb sphere at the very end and a small spike protruding from it to form the stinger point.

For the tail bands, I'm alternating amber and dark color segments at each joint to give a segmented look, with the dark color matching the bulb end for visual continuity, then moving on to the head shield — a flattened amber sphere positioned and scaled at the head joint.

Now I'm positioning the eye cluster on top of the head shield using small spheres, then working out the abdomen segments running backward from the core joint with gradually shrinking radii and flattened scaling to build a tapered scorpion-like body shape.

Setting up connecting rings between segments, then defining the leg joints -- hip points, foot positions, and leg lengths for four leg pairs -- with sweep thickness and bend angles to give the legs a bent, articulated look.

I'm naming each leg's joints (hip, knee, foot) per side and index, then making sure the leg chain parents correctly to the core at the right height. I'm also setting up the module exports with metadata, pulling in the needed SDK helpers (createBuilder, limb, catmull), and sketching out the claw/palm geometry with a sphere part scaled and positioned on the hand bone.

Now I'm placing the fingertip spheres with small dark tips, defining the curved paths for the fixed and moving pincer fingers so they meet near the hand joint and taper outward, and double-checking the head joint position relative to the arm base before starting the tail path from the core.

Working through the tail segments, rings, segment radii, and torus placements, then sketching the full build function covering joints, abdomen spheres, dark rings, head shield, eyes, legs via the limb helper, arms, pincers, and the tail with its stinger bulb. Writing build code...
